questions.question: What does the Mandela Fleming model aim to connect?
questions.answer: Exchange‑rate movements with monetary‑policy differences across countries
questions.explanation: The speaker says the model connects what moves the exchange rate and how different monetary policies affect it.

evidence.quote:
So what the Mandela Fleming model is about,
 it's about first connecting these things,
 trying to understand what moves the exchange rate, how
 different monetary policies in different places,
 or different policies in different places in the world,
 affect exchange rate.

options: Exchange‑rate movements with monetary‑policy differences across countries
Consumer confidence indices and stock market returns
Inflation rates within a single country
Long‑run fiscal deficits and trade balances

original_segments.text: So nobody expected the yen to move, to follow the US.
And while with respect to Europe,
well, Europe was having inflationary problems
and so on as well, so people expected it
to follow the US at some point.
For Japan, there was nothing like that.
And that's what led to the massive depreciation
of the gain, appreciation of the US dollar vis-a-vis again.
So what the Mandela Fleming model is about,
it's about first connecting these things,
trying to understand what moves the exchange rate, how
different monetary policies in different places,
or different policies in different places in the world,
affect exchange rate.
And then it's about understanding
how those exchange rate movements affect
real activity in the short run.
That's what the Mandela Fleming model is.
So it is really, we're gonna go back to our old ISLM model,
very short run, we're gonna even fix
nominal prices and so on.
So back to that environment,
but we're gonna do it in an open economy,
so we're gonna have a new variable floating around,
which is the exchange rate,
and we need to understand how the exchange rate moves
when different things happen in different countries,
and what is the impact of that on aggregate demand,
and hence on output, we're talking about the very short run,
in the different parts of the world.

questions.answer: Nobody expected the yen to move to follow the US
